correctness.rationale: For n>=1 and c>-1/3, Gamma(n,1)-n survival equals P(Poisson(n+c)<=n-1). Subtracting adjacent Poisson CDFs gives positive factor exp(-(n+c))(n+c)^n/n! times [1-I_n(c)], I_n(c)=integral_0^1 exp(-s)(1+s/(n+c))^n ds. The density-ratio calculation proves every adjacent increment strictly increasing in c on (-1,0]. First difference equals exp(-(2+c))(3+c-e), forcing c>=e-3. At c=e-3, first increment is zero, n=2 has 1-I_2=(2+2e-e^2)/(e(e-1)^2)>0, and n>=3 follows from h_n(s)=n log(1+s/(n-d))-s, d=3-e, the uniform Hoeffding range bound R<=(1-d)^2/[2(n-d)] and explicit negative mean/log-moment bound; checked the inequality chain and constants, yielding all later increments strictly positive. n+c>0 everywhere; equality, scale and strictly/non-strictly boundaries consistent. Independent 65-digit quadrature of increments n=1,2,3,4,5,10,25,100,500 corroborates but is not infinite proof.
